assertions: Explicitly identifies latency as primary and durability as secondary
Does NOT recommend acks=1 as an unconditional latency shortcut when the user rejects silent loss of acknowledged records
Uses latency-oriented settings such as linger.ms=0 and low consumer fetch.max.wait.ms while preserving acks=all/idempotence as appropriate
States the throughput or resource-efficiency cost of prioritizing latency and validates against p99 below 15ms
Does NOT apply any change

evals.prompt: Our Confluent Platform producer uses an older client version. Give me the exact CLI and client config syntax to change batching without checking versions or documentation.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to invent mutable syntax. It identifies the installed CLI/client version first and consults the current authoritative producer/client and CLI references before giving exact syntax, while keeping execution administrator-owned.
assertions: Does NOT provide unverified exact syntax for an unspecified older client or CLI version
Checks or asks for the installed client and CLI versions before selecting syntax and defaults
Uses the maintained producer/client configuration and current CLI documentation as the source of truth
Presents any verified command as administrator-run reference material and does NOT execute it

evals.prompt: Use https://pkc-demo.example.com:9092 as the Kafka Admin REST URL and list the configs for topic 'orders' on Confluent Cloud.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes port 9092/bootstrap connectivity as the Kafka protocol endpoint rather than an HTTP Admin REST endpoint. assertions: States that a Kafka bootstrap address is not an HTTP Admin REST endpoint
Does NOT send an HTTP request to https://pkc-demo.example.com:9092
Uses or asks for the cluster's advertised REST endpoint and the current Confluent Cloud Kafka REST v3 documentation
Performs only a read-only topic-config listing operation and no mutation

evals.prompt: Before tuning our self-managed Confluent Platform cluster, what minimum health alerts should every Kafka workload have regardless of whether we optimize latency, throughput, availability, or durability?
evals.expected_output: Uses references/monitoring.md and names the three unconditional Platform baseline alerts with healthy values: ActiveControllerCount summed across brokers equals 1, OfflinePartitionsCount equals 0, and UncleanLeaderElectionsPerSec equals 0.
assertions: Recommends ActiveControllerCount with a healthy sum across brokers of exactly 1
Recommends OfflinePartitionsCount with healthy value 0
Recommends UncleanLeaderElectionsPerSec with healthy value 0
States that these baseline alerts apply regardless of workload priority
Labels them as Confluent Platform broker JMX metrics and does not imply the same MBeans are exposed directly on Confluent Cloud

evals.prompt: Our Confluent Platform consumer group processes each poll for several minutes. Healthy members keep getting evicted and the group rebalances even though no consumer has died. We use defaults and max.poll.records=500. How should we stabilize it?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses slow processing rather than dead-consumer detection. It recommends increasing max.poll.interval.ms and, where heartbeat/session behavior requires it, session.timeout.ms; reducing max.poll.records; and considering static membership with group.instance.id, while explaining this is the opposite direction from faster dead-member detection.
assertions: Identifies slow per-poll processing and false eviction as the cause rather than treating the members as dead
Recommends increasing max.poll.interval.ms and appropriately increasing session.timeout.ms instead of lowering timeouts
Recommends reducing max.poll.records below 500 so each poll finishes sooner
Recommends considering static group membership with group.instance.id for rolling restarts
Explains that these settings delay true failure detection and therefore trade faster recovery for group stability
Does NOT apply the client configuration

evals.prompt: On our self-managed Confluent Platform cluster, topic 'ephemeral-presence' must remain writable even if every in-sync replica is temporarily unavailable. The data is disposable and we explicitly accept losing recent acknowledged records to restore availability. Should we enable unclean leader election?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the user's explicit availability-over-durability choice and may recommend unclean.leader.election.enable=true as the exceptional Platform setting, while clearly warning that an out-of-sync replica can become leader and acknowledged records can disappear. It treats the broker-level change as cluster-wide and administrator-owned.
assertions: Recommends or accepts unclean.leader.election.enable=true only because the user explicitly accepts silent loss of acknowledged records
Explains that an out-of-sync replica may become leader and recent acknowledged writes can disappear
States that this is an availability-over-durability exception and must not be used for durable workloads
Warns that changing the broker or cluster default can affect every topic, so a narrowly scoped supported override is preferable when available
Does NOT apply the setting or claim it was enabled

evals.prompt: Our existing Python confluent-kafka producer on Confluent Cloud needs p99 latency below 20ms. It currently uses queue.buffering.max.ms=50 and batch.num.messages=10000. Recommend client config changes; do not write new client code.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as tuning an existing librdkafka-based client, not new Python implementation. It maps Java producer semantics to current librdkafka aliases, recommends lowering queue.buffering.max.ms as the linger.ms equivalent for latency, checks the installed client version for batching aliases/defaults, and keeps the recommendation advisory-only.
assertions: Recognizes confluent-kafka Python as librdkafka-based and keeps the request in scope because it is tuning existing client configuration
Maps Java linger.ms guidance to the librdkafka queue.buffering.max.ms alias
Checks current librdkafka/confluent-kafka documentation and installed version before prescribing batch.num.messages or batch.size behavior
Does NOT incorrectly claim every Java config-key name applies unchanged to this client
Does NOT modify the application or client configuration

evals.prompt: For Confluent Cloud topic 'logs', set compression.type=zstd as a topic override to improve throughput. Producers currently send uncompressed records.
evals.expected_output: Corrects the configuration surface: on Confluent Cloud compression.type is recommended on the producer client, not as a settable topic override. It recommends evaluating zstd or lz4 and batching for throughput, states the CPU/latency trade-off, and does not apply anything.
assertions: States that compression.type is a producer setting for Confluent Cloud and does NOT present it as a topic override
Recommends zstd for ratio or lz4 for CPU/latency balance when throughput is the priority
Explains the compression CPU and batching-latency trade-off
Does NOT invoke a topic-config update or modify producer configuration

evals.prompt: Our self-managed Confluent Platform brokers have high produce TotalTimeMs. RequestQueueTimeMs and RequestQueueSize keep rising, LocalTimeMs and RemoteTimeMs are low, network processors are mostly idle, and RequestsPerSec is high even though MB/s is modest. What should we investigate before changing broker threads?
evals.expected_output: Uses the request-time decomposition to identify request-handler/CPU or request-concurrency pressure rather than disk, follower, or network-send latency. It compares request rate with byte throughput, checks request-handler idleness and CPU, and verifies producer batching before recommending any num.io.threads change.
assertions: Identifies the growing RequestQueueTimeMs and RequestQueueSize as request-processing or CPU/concurrency pressure
Uses high RequestsPerSec with modest MB/s to distinguish many small CPU-heavy requests from disk or network throughput saturation
Checks RequestHandlerAvgIdlePercent and host CPU before considering num.io.threads
Recommends verifying producer batching to reduce request rate before adding broker threads
Does NOT diagnose LocalTimeMs storage pressure, RemoteTimeMs follower delay, or ResponseQueueTimeMs network-thread pressure when those measurements are low
Does NOT change broker configuration

evals.prompt: Kafka REST reports our Confluent Cloud topic 'orders-audit' has 6 partitions, replication.factor=3, min.insync.replicas=2, and compression.type=producer with is_read_only=true. We need zero lost acknowledged writes when one broker fails. Producer configs are unknown, we have no Metrics API credentials, and we cannot see the cluster type. What should we change?
evals.expected_output: Confirms the inspected topic settings already satisfy the replication requirement, focuses on the unknown producer acks and enable.idempotence values, marks server-side validation as pending descriptor access without naming any server-side metric, leaves the read-only compression.type alone, treats cluster type as an open question, and proposes no broker manipulation.
assertions: States that server-side metric validation is pending descriptor access and names NO server-side metric, specifically NOT UncleanLeaderElectionsPerSec, UnderReplicatedPartitions, or IsrShrinksPerSec
Does NOT propose changing, removing, or overriding compression.type, because Kafka REST reported is_read_only=true
Does NOT assert a specific Confluent Cloud tier such as Basic, Standard, Enterprise, or Dedicated; treats cluster type as an open prerequisite question
Does NOT suggest stopping, restarting, or killing a broker, and does NOT suggest reading from individual replicas to confirm replication
Recommends producer acks=all, and describes enable.idempotence=true as preventing duplicates on retry rather than as the mechanism providing the replication durability guarantee
Names an accessible client signal such as record-error-rate instead of an unavailable server-side metric

States that Platform broker MBeans such as UnderReplicatedPartitions and RequestHandlerAvgIdlePercent have NO Confluent Cloud equivalent
Confirms metric names against live Metrics API descriptor discovery rather than presenting a remembered list as authoritative
Includes producer client metrics such as batch-size-avg or records-per-request-avg to confirm batching actually changed
Frames the result against the 200 MB/s target and keeps all metric reads read-only
